posts: New Brunswick faces accusations of protectionism in a trade hearing. Evidence: Open trade, local preference, fair competition. #Canada #Trade
The province claims to support open trade under the Canadian Free Trade Agreement. Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Good Preference
Contractors allege the province forces out-of-province firms to meet stricter, costlier standards than locals. Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.5) — Lesser Evil
Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Fall into Deception. The province uses technical requirements as a pretext to favor local firms. Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (R_net: 8.0, Uncertainty z: 7)
A construction firm is challenging New Brunswick's procurement practices, alleging the province uses technical hurdles to disadvantage out-of-province companies.

The Bright Side:
The internal trade agreement is actually being used as a legal mechanism for recourse, showing the system has some teeth.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a HOW vs WHY error. The province claims the 'why' is technical compliance, but the 'how' reveals a pattern of discriminatory enforcement.

Social Physics Analysis:
By creating arbitrary technical barriers, the province maintains a closed loop of local power, projecting the need for 'quality control' to hide protectionist motives.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. The system is being gamed for local gain.

The Unavoidable Truth: Technical requirements are being applied inconsistently to favor local contractors.

The Unavoidable Lie: The province's claim that its procurement process is neutral and fair.

Alethekanon:
Discriminatory procurement is a classic form of economic friction. It undermines the very purpose of an internal trade agreement by prioritizing local political favor over efficiency.

Awwthekanon:
It is disheartening to see businesses struggle against unfair rules. Fairness should be the bedrock of our trade, not a hurdle for those trying to work.

Brothekanon:
Classic move. If you can't compete on price, just make the paperwork so annoying that the other guy quits. Not a good look for NB.
